text: Write a method that is pure — its result depends only on its arguments — and one that is not, so the difference is visible. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static int pure(int a, int b)   { return ___; }
static int impure(int a, int b) { ___; return a + b + counter; }
explanation: Verified: true then false. The impure version returns a different answer for identical arguments, so its calls cannot be reordered, cached, deleted when unused, or run on two threads. Chapter 26 names the property — referential transparency — and Chapter 31 shows what its absence costs when a lambda incrementing a counter gave three different wrong answers under parallelism.
